Committee: Ways and Means General Fund
Sponsor: Clouse
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 09/27/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 4 as introduced authorizes the Alabama Corrections Institution Finance Authority (Authority) to issue up to $785 million in bonds to fund a phased plan for construction and renovation of prison facilities to replace existing bed space, which would increase the annual debt services obligations of the Authority by an estimated $50 million dollars for 30 years. This obligation would be offset by the rent received from the Alabama Department of Corrections (Department) for the lease of any facilities constructed or renovated from these bond proceeds, presumably funded from the State General Fund appropriation to the Department.
The phased construction and renovation of prison facilities by the Authority authorized by this bill includes the following:
Phase 1: construction of a mens facility in Escambia County, construction of a specialized mens facility in Elmore County, and closure of the Hamilton, Staton, Elmore, and Kilby facilities.  Following the closure of these facilities, provides for the Department to close the St. Clair Correctional Facility;
Phase 2: construction of a womens facility in Elmore County, closure of the Tutwiler facility,  and renovation or demolition and reconstruction of certain existing mens facilities;
Phase 3: evaluation of the mens facilities to determine if additional beds need to be replaced.
Further, this bill provides for the awarding of the contracts for design and construction of the mens facility in Escambia County and specialized mens facility in Elmore County. This bill also provides that all other construction contemplated by this bill shall be subject to the current
statutory public works bid requirements and authorizes the authority to negotiate with bidders on such construction, when multiple bids are received, and all of the bids exceed the available funding.
Further, this bill creates the Department of Corrections  Correctional Capital Improvement Fund and the Correctional Facilities Maintenance Fund within the State Treasury to be administered by the Department. This bill requires the Legislature to appropriate funds 1) to the former to be used exclusively for the construction, renovation, and improvement of prison facilities pursuant to the phased prison construction and renovation program authorized by this bill; and 2) to the latter to be exclusively for maintenance of prison facilities constructed under the provisions of this bill.
In addition, this bill could also increase receipts to the Correctional Facilities Maintenance Fund by an undetermined amount dependent upon the proceeds received from by the Authority from the sale, conveyance, or lease of all or any part of real and personal property that is not being used by the DOC, as authorized by this bill.
Further, this bill would also increase the obligations of the State General Fund to lease or purchase the prison facility in Perry County. House Bill 6 of the 2021 1st Extraordinary Session appropriates $19 million for this purpose.
Further, this bill provides that the Authority submit a report to the Legislature within 30 days of the completion of any bond sale.  The Authority is required to develop a plan that encourages minority business participation in the construction of prison facilities must administer training programs and other educational activities and submit a quarterly report to the Governor and Legislature on minority participation. This will increase the obligations of the Authority by an undetermined amount to comply with the provisions of this bill.
Further, this bill authorizes the Authority to delegate its administrative or reporting duties and obligations to DOC or any other state entity, which would increase the administrative obligations of that state entity.
Finally, this bill adds the following four members to the Authority: 1) the Chair of the House Ways and Means-General Fund Committee; 2) the Chair of the Senate Finance and Taxation-General Fund Committee; 3) a joint appointment by the House and Senate Minority Leaders; and 4) the Director of the Bureau of Pardons and Paroles.
Steve Clouse, Chair
Ways and Means General Fund
